review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Fasteners, screw threads, washers, installation actions, wrenches, clamps, and a newly exposed upper-graph exclusion conflict.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. NASA RP-1228 (Richard T. Barrett, 1990; US Government public-use work) supports qualitative fastener distinctions only. Current manufacturer material and tool evidence corrects narrow dictionary assumptions. No design standards, torque values, installation procedures or product advice are imported.
review.context_policy: All new assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Existing home contexts and grammar remain unchanged; the IT build record is not moved into physical assembly.

sense_decisions.scope: A fastener whose function uses a screw thread, including screws, bolts and threaded nuts. No one head shape or material is required.
A physical helical surface feature on or inside a part. Extend the external-rib-only dictionary gloss to include internal threads; not textile thread or an execution thread.
A screw thread on the outer surface of a part. No pitch, profile, handedness or tolerance class is imposed.
A screw thread on an internal surface, such as in a nut. No specific thread standard is imposed.

sense_decisions.alignment: engineering sense absent from the selected dictionary washer cluster
sense_decisions.scope: A washer used in a fastening assembly. Model it as a component, not a washing appliance, worker or necessarily a leak-sealing gasket.
A flat washer used under fastening hardware; no sealing or anti-loosening guarantee is asserted.
A washer designed to exhibit spring action under axial compression. Its actual fastening performance depends on the assembly.
A split helical spring washer. Its name is not evidence that every assembly is protected from loosening.
A nut with a hexagonal external wrenching form; no material or grade is imposed.
A nut with projections for finger turning. Exclude the tree sense and the misleading wing-screw synonym for this nut.
A nut used against another nut or mating part to resist relative movement. This is the jam-nut meaning, not every self-locking nut.
A nut with crown slots that accommodate a retaining pin in a suitable assembly. The unattached nut need not include that pin as a component.
A screw used to secure a part against relative movement, for example on a shaft. Headlessness is common but not universal; exclude the separate spring-tension-adjustment sense.
A screw using the Phillips drive form. Do not equate every cross-shaped recess, including Pozidriv, with Phillips.
A screw with an internal hexagonal driving recess, distinct from an external hexagon head.
A screw whose body is steel; this material-defined subtype receives the former broad steel assertion.
A nail with a steel body; do not generalize this material to every nail.
A driven nail made from wood. The manufacturer evidence establishes that nails need not be metal; no proprietary performance or installation rule is generalized.
A fastener set by deforming part of it to secure an assembly. Broaden the solid-pin-and-hammer gloss to cover the reviewed blind-rivet family.
A rivet with a solid shank before setting; no single material or forming tool is mandatory.
A rivet designed for installation with access from one side. Not all blind rivets use a pull mandrel; drive-pin and threaded-stem forms exist.
A blind rivet set by pulling a mandrel. Distinct from the full blind-rivet family, which has other installation mechanisms.
A pin fitted into aligned holes to locate or retain parts. Restrict the broad dowel cluster; exclude a loose rod, a display pin and PIN authentication.
A split retaining pin whose legs can be spread after insertion. The unsplit tapered cotter is a different hardware type.
A device intended to hold a physical object. It is distinct from possession, emotional attachment and an intellectual grasp.
A clamp with a C-shaped frame. No universal frame material or force rating is asserted.
A clamp whose gripping force is supplied by a spring; not every clamp uses a threaded spindle.
A vise intended for mounting at a workbench; distinguish the narrower dictionary bench-vise cluster from the existing general vise record.
A screwdriver for the Phillips drive. Do not claim compatibility with every cross-head system.
A wrench with an adjustable jaw opening.
A wrench whose ring-like working end fits around a fastener head or nut.
A wrench that drives through a socket-shaped working end. Sockets may be integral or interchangeable; a ratchet is not mandatory.
A key that engages an internal hexagonal recess. Do not import every brand name from the synset as a generic alias.
Installing or securing threaded fastening hardware by rotation; narrower than the action that can also screw on a lid.
Loosening or removing threaded fastening hardware by rotation; do not require a complete removal or a universal clockwise direction.
Riveting by setting pull-mandrel blind rivets; not every blind riveting process uses this mechanism.
A manually operated tool for setting pull-mandrel blind rivets. Distinguish this from rivet-nut tools, powered riveting machines and the riveter occupation.
Fastening with nails. Do not require a hand hammer; suitable nailers also perform the process.
Broaden the English label to physical tool and reject the unsupported material percentage and false dishware exclusion.
Reuse screw fastener; do not copy tapered-shank and slotted-head restrictions to all screws.
Reuse nail fastener, allowing documented nonmetal nail bodies.
Reuse nut (fastener) already distinct from edible nut 3210.
Correct the malformed unscrewing action rather than create a duplicate general action.
Explicitly select riveting, retain original lookup, and specialize the physical-action genus through fastening.
Keep vise broad; add a bench-vise subtype rather than assert all vises are workbench-mounted.
Defer the chemical-compound/physical-joining conflation; do not attach fasteners to this mixed record.
Twisting off can include detachment without a screw thread; do not automatically merge it with unscrewing.
The generated Russian perfective metalworking record needs a full duplicate/sense review.
Review pincers versus broader pliers and cutting-only pliers before adding hand-tool subtypes.
The dictionary washer entry selects a sealing gasket; do not import that genus for all fastening washers.
A screwdriver cocktail is not a tool.
A spring-tension adjusting setscrew is not automatically the selected shaft-securing setscrew sense.
A wing-nut tree is not fastening hardware.
A screw propeller is not the selected fastening screw.
A jewelry pin is not automatically a locating dowel pin.

review.limits: Qualitative vocabulary only. Thread geometry tolerances, pitch/lead, torque, load ratings, material grades, safety and national standards are outside scope. The cloth/PIN/thread and figurative screw/nut senses are not merged. Pliers/pincers, physical gripping duplicates, attaching/fastening generated leaves, compound/joining record 3488, and remaining U1 exclusion conflicts need separate review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Reject the tool/dishware and action/process exclusions; retain meaningful multiple genera. Other 20 pre-existing candidates remain for individual review.
exclusion_review.regression: After application, no conflict edge or witness may be newly introduced by Q18; save a private witness comparison.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Exact normalized English spellings are candidates, not semantic identities or a missing-concept count.
